diffs.diff: humidity_%RH: datasheet reading gives 1 per count, the part's model has none
diffs.evidence: Aosong DHT11 datasheet (p.7): 'Data format: 8bit humidity integer data + 8bit humidity decimal data + 8bit temperature integer data + 8bit temperature decimal data + 8bit check bit. Note: the humidity fraction is 0.' So humidity = the integer byte, 1 %RH per count, offset 0 -- the same as the second reading. The model is not wrong: it is sim kind 'dht-sensor', which has no measure/responses scale field (the comparator finds 'none'); its humidity control is in %RH and the simulator (src/sim/engine.ts dhtRead) hands the integer value straight to MicroPython's dht.DHT11 class, which decodes the humidity byte as 1 %RH per count. The example test (humidity 72 -> 'H=72%') confirms the 1:1 mapping.

diffs.diff: temperature_C: datasheet reading gives 1 per count, the part's model has none
diffs.evidence: Aosong DHT11 datasheet (p.7): '8bit temperature integer data + 8bit temperature decimal data'; 'The temperature is high as part of the data of the temperature... the temperature low bit 8 is the negative temperature'. So temperature = the integer byte, 1 degC per count, offset 0 -- matching the second reading. The model's sim kind 'dht-sensor' has no scale field to compare; its 'value' slider is in degC (0-50) and is passed 1:1 to MicroPython's dht.DHT11 decoder, as the passing example test (value 34 -> 'T=34C') shows. The model's build note already says MicroPython's DHT11 class does not decode the sub-zero sign bit, which is why the range is 0-50 degC.
